entries.title: 30 more player skins — Dream SMP, MCC & YouTubers
entries.summary: PlayerMobs can now spawn wearing 30 additional real-player skins from the Minecraft streaming and MCC scene — Dream, Technoblade, CaptainSparklez, LDShadowLady, Skeppy and more — bringing the custom-skin pool to 68. Recognizable real-player skins also show up more often: a naturally-spawned PlayerMob now has a 40% chance (up from 30%) of wearing one instead of a vanilla default.
highlights: 30 new skins (pool now 68): Dream SMP, MCC players, and Minecraft YouTubers
Recognizable real-player skins now appear ~40% of the time, up from ~30%
Each skin renders with its correct slim or wide arm model

entries.title: Loved PlayerMobs travel with you on the Dungeon Train
entries.summary: On a Dungeon Train, a PlayerMob that has come to love you now abandons its own fixed route and makes its way to your carriage, settling in once it's with you. Move on down the train and it follows; step off the train and it stays aboard and goes back to its usual wandering.
highlights: A PlayerMob that loves you heads to your carriage instead of marching its own way
Uses the full train toolkit to reach you — stepping through rooms, leaping carriage-group gaps, opening doors, and digging through fill
Relaxes and does its own thing once it shares your carriage; resumes its route if you leave the train
Toggle with the new trainFollowLovedPlayer config option (on by default)

entries.title: Reincarnated echoes wear the player's real skin
entries.summary: "Echo of <name>" PlayerMobs on the Dungeon Train now show the real skin of the player they're an echo of, instead of a default Steve/Alex skin. Their name was already right — now their look matches too.
highlights: Dungeon-Train echoes match the skin of the player they came from
Also fixes the friend-echoes that travel alongside them
The skin is captured at the moment of death, so each echo looks like that player did then

entries.title: Reincarnations can come from other mods
entries.summary: PlayerMob now has a two-way reincarnation bridge other mods can plug into: a companion mod can both add past lives — including players from other worlds — to the pool a PlayerMob may return as, and read PlayerMob's death log. Local and remote reincarnations roll on separate chances, so meeting players from elsewhere never reduces your chance of meeting your own past lives. With no such mod installed nothing changes — except that Dungeon Train echoes now lean toward your more recent past lives.
highlights: Other mods can contribute past lives to the reincarnation pool — a spawning PlayerMob can come back as a life from an integrating mod, not just PlayerMob's own death log.
Players from other worlds can turn up as echoes in yours (and you in theirs) — a remote echo is always someone else, never you.
Local and remote echoes roll separately, so a remote pool never eats into your own past-life reincarnations.
Other mods can read PlayerMob's death log (who died, where, and their skin, gear and traits).
Dungeon Train echoes now favour your more recent deaths, with a mild lean toward lives that ended near your current depth.

entries.title: Integration seam to steer a PlayerMob's train march
entries.summary: Adds a small compatibility seam (TrainConfinement.setMarchDirection) that lets a Dungeon-Train host set a freshly-spawned PlayerMob's fixed march direction along the train, overriding its normal boarding choice. PlayerMob's own behaviour is unchanged; Dungeon Train uses this so a PlayerMob can be spawned already heading your way.
highlights: New compat API: TrainConfinement.setMarchDirection(mob, dir) plus PlayerMobEntity.setTrainExploreDir(int).

entries.title: Echo-spawn modding seam
entries.summary: Adds a modding hook so an integrating mod can react the moment a PlayerMob spawns as a reincarnated echo — Dungeon Train uses it to chronicle cross-world echo encounters.
highlights: New PlayerMobSpawnHooks seam reports each echo spawn with its source life and whether it came from a local or remote (cross-world) pool.

entries.title: Personality now colours how PlayerMobs feel about you
entries.summary: A PlayerMob's friendliness and aggression now shape how strongly it reacts to you, not just how it behaves. The friendlier a mob, the more it warms to acts of kindness — gifts, bows, and being defended land harder. The more aggressive a mob, the less it cares about being struck — a hot-tempered fighter shrugs off a blow that would turn a gentler mob against you.
highlights: Friendly mobs warm up to twice as fast from gifts, bows, and rescues (×1.0 at minimum friendliness rising to ×2.0 at maximum).
Aggressive mobs barely hold a grudge for being hit, while timid mobs take it to heart (×0.2 at maximum aggression up to ×1.2 at minimum).
The Aggressive archetype is now both hard to befriend and slow to anger when struck; the Friendly archetype bonds quickly but is more easily hurt.

entries.title: PlayerMob now runs on Minecraft 1.20.1
entries.summary: PlayerMob now ships a build for Minecraft 1.20.1 (Fabric and Forge), alongside the existing 1.21.1 build. It's the same player-shaped, weapon-aware mob — now playable on 1.20.1 worlds.
highlights: New 1.20.1 build for Fabric and Forge.
NeoForge 1.20.1 users: the Forge jar works on NeoForge 1.20.1.
1.21.1 builds (Fabric, Forge, NeoForge) are unchanged — grab the jar matching your Minecraft version + loader.

entries.title: PlayerMob now runs on the latest Minecraft (26.2)
entries.summary: PlayerMob now ships a build for Minecraft 26.2 'Chaos Cubed' (Fabric and NeoForge), on top of the existing 1.20.1 and 1.21.1 builds. It's the same player-shaped, weapon-aware mob — now on the latest Minecraft.
highlights: New 26.2 build for Fabric and NeoForge.
PlayerMob now covers Minecraft 1.20.1, 1.21.1, and 26.2 — grab the jar matching your version + loader.
NeoForge 26.2 is still in beta upstream, so treat the 26.2 build as a preview.

entries.title: Adventure Item Names now bundled in
entries.summary: PlayerMob now ships with Adventure Item Names built in on Minecraft 1.21.1 (Fabric, Forge, and NeoForge) — no separate download. Naturally-spawned swords, tools, shields, and armor get procedural names out of the box, and the two mods coordinate so reincarnated echo mobs keep their own names.
highlights: Auto-installs alongside PlayerMob on MC 1.21.1 — no extra file to grab
Turn it off anytime: set Adventure Item Names' naming chance to 0 in its config, or remove the bundled mod
1.20.1 and 26.2 builds are unaffected (not bundled there yet)

entries.title: Natural spawning — PlayerMobs appear in the wild
entries.summary: PlayerMobs can now spawn naturally in your world, off by default. When enabled, a PlayerMob has a configurable chance to appear alongside a normally-spawning mob (the mob is never replaced), with sensible per-group defaults — and villages can be settled by PlayerMobs among their villagers.
highlights: Opt-in: set naturalSpawnEnabled=true in config/playermob.properties (ships off).
Spawns BESIDE the mob, never replacing it — works for hostiles, nether mobs, animals, water, and villages.
Per-group default chances: Hostile 0.0, Nether 0.05, Animals 0.15, Friendly 0.15, Water 0.0, Villager 0.25 — each mob also tunable individually.
Villages: ~1/4 of villagers (and structure iron golems) get a PlayerMob companion.
Tune it live without a restart: /playermob naturalspawn on|off, /playermob naturalspawn <mob> on|off|<chance>, and /playermob naturalspawn group <group> on|off|<chance>.

entries.title: Custom skins by player name
entries.summary: Mob-pack authors can now add a PlayerMob skin by simply naming a player — PlayerMob looks up that player's real skin (and arm model) automatically, so you no longer need to hunt down a texture URL. You can also summon a PlayerMob wearing a specific player's skin in-game, and mods can feed skins in through a new API.
highlights: Datapack skins accept "playerName" instead of a "textureUrl" — the skin is resolved for you on /reload.
New command: /playermob summon <player> [<pos>] [<friendliness>] [<fightFlight>] spawns a PlayerMob wearing that player's skin (traits optional, default random).
Modders can add skins via the new SkinSources API.
Name lookups need internet and are cached; unknown names or an offline server fall back to a bundled skin. Pre-resolved textureUrl entries still work offline.

entries.title: Adventure Item Names: switch from bundled to suggested dependency
entries.summary: Adventure Item Names is no longer bundled inside PlayerMob's jar. It is now declared as a suggested dependency in the mod metadata, letting launchers and users manage the AIN version themselves. Existing users upgrading from a JiJ version will need to install AIN separately if they want its item-naming features.

entries.title: Fixed PlayerMob crashing on startup on Forge 1.20.1
entries.summary: PlayerMob now loads on Forge 1.20.1. Previously the mod crashed the game on startup the instant it loaded, making it unusable on that version. The startup crash — and a second crash that surfaced right after it, where the spawn eggs failed to register — are both fixed. PlayerMob now loads, summons, and all six spawn eggs work on Forge 1.20.1. Forge 1.21.1, NeoForge, and Fabric were never affected.
highlights: Forge 1.20.1 no longer crashes on startup when PlayerMob is installed
The PlayerMob spawn egg and the five archetype eggs now register and work on Forge 1.20.1
No change to Forge 1.21.1, NeoForge, or Fabric

entries.title: Fixed PlayerMob rendering on the "latest" (MC 26.2) build
entries.summary: The "latest" (Minecraft 26.2) build is now usable. Previously every PlayerMob rendered as the default Steve skin, the spawn-egg icons were missing (the purple-and-black "missing texture" checkerboard), the client could crash the moment a PlayerMob came into view, and the right-click editor menu in Creative was garbled. All four are fixed: PlayerMobs show their real, varied skins again, the spawn eggs show their proper coloured icons, rendering no longer crashes, and the editor menu lays out correctly. MC 1.20.1 and 1.21.1 were never affected.
highlights: PlayerMobs on MC 26.2 show their real, varied skins again instead of all looking like Steve
Spawn-egg icons show their proper colours instead of the missing-texture checkerboard
Fixed a client crash that could fire when a PlayerMob came into view on 26.2
The right-click editor menu (Creative) renders correctly again on 26.2 — relationship portraits show as placeholder squares there for now

entries.title: Personality spawn eggs keep their archetype on MC 1.20.1
entries.summary: On Minecraft 1.20.1, the personality spawn eggs (Aggressive, Friendly, Passive, Skeptical, Shy) were spawning random PlayerMobs instead of their intended personality. They now reliably spawn a mob with the egg's archetype — both from the creative menu and from /give.
highlights: Aggressive, Friendly, Passive, Skeptical and Shy eggs now pin their fight/flight + friendliness on 1.20.1, like they already did on newer versions.
Works however you get the egg — creative inventory, /give, or pick-block.

entries.title: PlayerMobs use real ammo for bows and crossbows
entries.summary: Archers now draw from their own quiver: a PlayerMob fires its bow or crossbow only while it carries ammo it can use, spending one round per shot. Bows use arrows; crossbows use arrows or firework rockets. Run it dry and it stops shooting — switching to a melee weapon, or darting over to grab nearby loose ammo when the enemy isn't right on top of it, then picking the weapon back up. It still favours ranged at a distance and closes to melee up close, and reloads crossbows between shots.
highlights: Bows and crossbows consume ammo from the mob's inventory — arrows for both, plus firework rockets for crossbows; no ammo means no shooting
Out of ammo mid-fight, it grabs nearby dropped arrows/fireworks (if the enemy isn't too close) or falls back to melee
Keeps the ranged-at-distance / melee-up-close behaviour and crossbow reloading
Toggle global unlimited ammo live with /playermob unlimitedammo on|off (or the requireArrows config), plus tunable engage distances

entries.title: Relationship faces render again on the latest MC build
entries.summary: On the newest Minecraft build, the PlayerMob editor's relationship list was drawing a blank grey square instead of each remembered individual's face. Real faces are back — every row shows the actual skin (head + hat overlay) again, matching the 1.20.1 and 1.21.1 versions.
highlights: Real per-skin faces restored in the relationship list on the latest MC build
Head and hat-overlay both render, identical to older versions

entries.title: Aggression sets how fast a PlayerMob fires its bow or crossbow
entries.summary: A PlayerMob's ranged firerate now follows its fight-or-flight nature. Brave mobs loose arrows and bolts as fast as the weapon can draw or charge; even-tempered ones pause a beat between shots; timid ones (which usually flee anyway) fire only rarely. The weapon's own draw/charge time is always the floor — nobody shoots faster than the bow allows.
highlights: Fearless mobs fire at the weapon's full speed
Average mobs add a ~2-second pause between shots
Timid mobs fire slowly on the rare occasion they stand and fight
Applies to both bows and crossbows

entries.title: Configurable extra pickup items
entries.summary: PlayerMobs can now be told to scoop up extra items they'd normally ignore. List item ids and/or item tags in the new extraPickupItems config line and the mob will grab them off the ground and out of chests, stashing them in its backpack — perfect for modded loot like a gun mod's ammo.
highlights: New extraPickupItems setting in playermob.properties — list item ids (scguns:assault_rifle) and/or tags (#scguns:ammo), comma or space separated
Configured items are picked up from the floor AND looted from chests, alongside the weapons, armor, ammo and valuables the mob already collects
Empty by default — no change unless you opt in; supports any mod's items

entries.title: Name your summoned PlayerMobs
entries.summary: The /playermob summon command can now give the spawned mob a floating nameplate, not just a player's skin. Append 'named' to use the same name as the skin, or 'named <yourname>' to set a different label.
highlights: /playermob summon Steve named — spawns with Steve's skin and a 'Steve' nameplate
/playermob summon Steve named Bob — Steve's skin, but the nameplate reads 'Bob' (multi-word names work too)
The flag tacks onto any existing form, e.g. /playermob summon Steve ~ ~ ~ 8 2 named

entries.title: Command PlayerMobs with /playermob order
entries.summary: A new op command lets you order a specific PlayerMob — by name, or the nearest one — to perform an action against a player, another PlayerMob, a mob type, or coordinates. The mob walks up, does the thing, then returns to its normal behaviour.
highlights: walk to, punch, taunt (punchat), or greet a target
attack with a stop limit — once, until dead, for N seconds, until N hearts, or until it's hit back — optionally with a chosen or conjured weapon
gift an auto-picked or specified item, and steal a target's held item then flee for a time or distance
use any item with a real right-click — place, till, shear, milk, buckets — working with modded items too
place a block at a spot, or have the mob chase a live player and place it at their feet

entries.title: PlayerMobs now visibly swing their arms
entries.summary: PlayerMobs weren't playing their arm-swing animation — punches, attacks, and the /playermob order actions looked static. They now swing like a real player, and an ordered punchat throws 2–6 punch motions facing you.
highlights: arm swings now animate in combat and for every order action
punchat faces you and throws 2–6 visible punches

entries.title: Drop-in local skin folder
entries.summary: PlayerMobs can now wear your own skins. Drop PNG skin files into config/playermob/skins and they join the random rotation alongside the built-in and online skins — slim (Alex) and wide (Steve) arms are detected automatically. You can also spawn a PlayerMob wearing a specific skin by filename, and turn each skin source on or off.
highlights: Drop .png skins in config/playermob/skins — used automatically on random spawns
Slim vs wide arms auto-detected from the skin file
/playermob summon <skin> — spawn a PlayerMob wearing a specific local skin (same command as a named-player summon)
/playermob skin sources and /playermob skin source <bundled|online|local> on|off — see and toggle which skin sources are used

entries.title: Naturally-spawned PlayerMobs can be named after their skin
entries.summary: Turn on auto-naming and every PlayerMob that spawns out in the world wears a nameplate showing where its look came from — the filename of your local skin, or the name behind an online skin. Mobs using a built-in default skin stay unnamed.
highlights: New 'autoNameNaturalSpawns' config option (off by default)
Toggle it live in-game with /playermob autonamenaturalspawns on|off
Local skins show their filename; online skins show their display name

entries.title: Choose which PlayerMobs get named after their skin
entries.summary: Auto-naming is now a mode instead of an on/off switch. Pick which kinds of spawns wear their skin source as a nameplate — wild spawns, egg/spawner/command spawns, all of them, or none.
highlights: /playermob autoname off|natural|egg|all (off by default)
'egg' covers spawn eggs, mob spawners, /summon and dispensers; 'natural' covers wild spawns; 'all' covers everything except Dungeon Train
/playermob summon <name|file> now waits for the skin to load before naming, and an explicit 'named' always takes priority

entries.title: Tune how often PlayerMobs wear a custom skin
entries.summary: The chance a PlayerMob spawns wearing a real custom skin (instead of a bundled vanilla default) is now yours to set. It still defaults to ~40%, exactly as before — but you can dial it anywhere from 0% (always a plain vanilla look) to 100% (always a custom skin, whenever one is available).
highlights: New config option customSkinChance (0.0-1.0) in config/playermob.properties — defaults to 0.4, so nothing changes unless you want it to.
Adjust it live without a restart: /playermob skin chance <0.0-1.0>.
/playermob skin sources now also shows the current custom-skin chance.
0.0 = every PlayerMob wears a bundled vanilla default; 1.0 = always a custom (online or local) skin when one exists; bundled stays the fallback when none is available.

entries.title: Unit tests now run on every supported Minecraft version
entries.summary: The mod's unit-test suite now runs automatically across all supported Minecraft versions (1.20.1, 1.21.1, and the 26.x preview) on every change, so cross-version regressions get caught before a build ever ships.

entries.title: Per-mob natural-spawn chances now work (and no more world-gen freeze)
entries.summary: Per-mob natural-spawn chances set in playermob.properties (e.g. naturalSpawnScale.minecraft:zombie) were silently ignored — every mob fell back to its group default, so custom values you set never applied. They now load correctly from your existing config, no edits needed. This also fixes a world-generation freeze that could happen when a village generated while natural spawning was on.
highlights: Per-mob naturalSpawnScale.<id> overrides now actually take effect (they were all being dropped)
Fixes a world-gen hang when villages/iron golems generated with natural spawning enabled
Works with your existing config file — no changes required

entries.title: Better Combat / Better Mob Combat support
entries.summary: Give a PlayerMob a sword or axe and it fights with Better Combat's animated wind-up and combo swings, like any other humanoid mob — works out of the box with Better Combat + Better Mob Combat (now listed as optional dependencies). Modpack heads-up: pair Better Mob Combat 1.3.0 with Better Combat 1.8.6, as the newer Better Combat 1.9.0 crashes.
highlights: PlayerMobs use Better Combat's animated melee when Better Combat + Better Mob Combat are installed
Pair Better Mob Combat 1.3.0 with Better Combat 1.8.6 — the newer 1.9.0 crashes

entries.title: PlayerMobs turn bomber with TNT
entries.summary: A PlayerMob that's carrying TNT and a way to light it now fights with explosives: it rushes whoever it's fighting, drops a stick of TNT, sets it off, and sprints clear — again and again until it runs out, then falls back to its usual bow-and-blade combat.
highlights: Lights the TNT with flint & steel or a fire charge, or by rigging a redstone block, lever, button, or pressure plate right beside it
Backs off just far enough to survive the blast, then comes straight back — no waiting around for the boom
Won't drop its TNT — or the tools to light it — when you kill it
On by default (needs the mobGriefing gamerule); toggle live with /playermob tntcombat on|off

entries.title: PlayerMobs bomb with end crystals from behind cover
entries.summary: A PlayerMob that's carrying end crystals, obsidian, and a few blocks to hide behind now fights with the game's biggest handheld explosion: it plants a crystal on an obsidian base by its target, throws up a little wall to duck behind, raises a shield if it has one, and punches the crystal to set it off — walking away from its own blast and doing it again until it runs out, then falling back to its usual bow-and-blade combat.
highlights: Stacks a two-block wall between itself and the crystal and crouches behind it (blocking with a shield if it has one), so it survives a point-blank blast while whoever it's fighting does not
Sets the crystal off with a real melee punch, and builds its little bunker one block at a time
Tries several angles when it rigs, so it works on hills and in tight spots, not just open flats
On by default (needs the mobGriefing gamerule); toggle live with /playermob endcrystalcombat on|off

entries.title: PlayerMob drops absolutely everything on death
entries.summary: A PlayerMob's death now drops its full backpack with zero exceptions — TNT, end crystals, obsidian, and igniters included, on top of its already-guaranteed equipped gear (weapon, off-hand, armor). Killing a bomber no longer withholds its explosives kit; it drops the whole thing, exactly like a player.
highlights: TNT and its igniters (flint & steel, fire charge, redstone block, lever, button, pressure plate) now drop on death instead of being withheld
End crystals and their obsidian base now drop on death instead of being withheld
Equipped gear and ordinary backpack items are unaffected — already dropped at 100% before this fix

entries.title: Summon a PlayerMob wearing a named player's skin via NBT
entries.summary: A raw /summon (or entity egg) can now carry a SkinPlayerName tag to wear a named player's real skin, composable with any other NBT (attributes, health, etc.) in the same command.
highlights: Local skin-folder files still take priority; otherwise the name is resolved against a real Mojang skin, same as /playermob summon

entries.title: PlayerMobs stop attacking neutral mobs unprovoked
entries.summary: PlayerMobs used to charge and attack zombified piglins on sight. Now they leave neutral mobs — zombified piglins, endermen, piglins, iron golems — alone unless the mob turns hostile first, just like these mobs leave players alone until provoked. PlayerMobs still defend themselves when attacked, and still hunt genuinely hostile mobs like zombies and skeletons.
highlights: Zombified piglins, endermen and piglins are no longer attacked on sight
PlayerMobs still fight back if a neutral mob turns on them
Genuinely hostile mobs (zombies, skeletons, creepers…) are still engaged as before

entries.title: Orders stick until they're done
entries.summary: Commands you give a PlayerMob (walk, greet, gift, steal, use, place, punch) no longer get forgotten if they take a while or the mob is interrupted. The mob now keeps the task and finishes it — reacting to threats along the way and picking the order back up afterward.
highlights: Orders persist until executed, instead of being dropped after ~10 seconds
By default the mob fights or flees a threat mid-task, then resumes the order
New flags: 'for <n> s' sets how long to keep trying, 'forever' never gives up, 'nonstop' ignores distractions
Each mob remembers its own default timeout / interruptibility (settable via NBT)

entries.title: Burning PlayerMobs run for water — or douse themselves with a bucket
entries.summary: A PlayerMob that catches fire now drops everything to save itself. If there's water close by it sprints in; if it's carrying a water bucket it dumps it at its feet, stands in the puddle to put the flames out, then scoops the water back up once it's safe. It won't get distracted or give up until it's no longer burning.
highlights: Sprints straight to nearby water the instant it catches fire, ignoring everything else until it's safe
Carrying a water bucket (in hand or backpack)? It empties it at its own feet, douses itself, then picks the water back up
On by default — toggle with /playermob extinguishwithbucket on|off, or the extinguishWithBucket config option

entries.title: PlayerMobs can wield modded firearms like MusketMod muskets
entries.summary: PlayerMobs can now use guns from other mods — muskets, pistols and the like — not just vanilla bows and crossbows. Point them at a supported firearm in the new moddedRangedWeapons config and a mob will pick it up, keep it, draw it when an enemy is at range, and fire it with the mod's own bullets. Just like a real musketeer, it stops to reload before every shot (with the mod's reload animation and sounds), then fires. It draws from real ammo it's carrying, so it falls back to melee when it runs dry.
highlights: Off by default — an admin lists the guns and their ammo in the moddedRangedWeapons config; MusketMod is the tested reference (all variants: musket, bayonet, scope, blunderbuss, pistol)
Full reload before every shot, using the mod's own loading animation and sounds — no instant firing

Fires the mod's real projectile and spends real ammo; works with any mod's firearm without extra code, and mobs can be armed via /item replace (mainhand gun + offhand cartridges) or by picking guns and ammo off the floor

entries.title: Keep a PlayerMob near a spot or companion (stay-near tether)
entries.summary: PlayerMobs can now be tethered so they won't wander off. Give a mob a stay-near anchor — a fixed position or a live entity (you or another PlayerMob) — plus a radius, and it stays within it: when it drifts (or gets dragged by a fight) past the edge, it walks back, then goes right back to doing its own thing inside the ring.
highlights: New command: /playermob stay <name> ( off | here | <pos> | <target> ) [radius] — default radius 32 blocks (1–256).
The tether yields to combat — a mob will chase an enemy past its ring, then walk back to its anchor once the fight is over.
The anchor survives save/load and can be baked into spawn NBT (PlayerMobData/StayNear), so summoned or egg-spawned mobs can come pre-tethered.

entries.title: New setting to stop PlayerMobs from hunting animals
entries.summary: Hungry PlayerMobs hunt nearby cows, pigs, chickens, sheep, and rabbits for meat when they're low on food. That's now optional — admins can turn it off entirely if they'd rather their PlayerMobs leave the local wildlife alone.
highlights: On by default, matching existing behaviour — toggle live with /playermob huntforfood on|off, or set huntForFood=false in the config to disable it permanently
Turning it off mid-hunt makes the mob drop the chase immediately, even with an animal already targeted

entries.title: Summon PlayerMobs pre-tethered — stay option, spawn NBT, and player-name anchors
entries.summary: You can now tether a PlayerMob the moment you summon it, instead of only after it already exists. /playermob summon gains a 'stay' option that pins the new mob to where it spawns, to a set of coordinates, or to a player or another PlayerMob — each with an optional radius. A new AnchorPlayer name key lets you tether by player name in spawn NBT, so you no longer need a raw UUID or a packed coordinate number; the mob follows that player as they move and reconnects to them after a relog. And /playermob summon now accepts raw {NBT} to bake in traits, skin, and the tether in one go.
highlights: New: /playermob summon <name> stay ( off | here | <pos> | <target> ) [radius] — tether a mob the instant it spawns
Tether by player NAME in spawn NBT via the new AnchorPlayer key — a friendly alternative to a raw UUID or a packed AnchorPos coordinate
Player/entity anchors follow the same leash-not-glue behaviour: the mob yields to combat, then walks back once it drifts beyond the radius
Optional {NBT} on /playermob summon bakes in traits, skin, and the stay tether at spawn

entries.title: Player-name skins now apply reliably on spawn eggs
entries.summary: Giving a PlayerMob a specific player's skin through a spawn egg's SkinPlayerName tag now works every time. Previously the skin would occasionally come out as a random player instead of the one you asked for.
highlights: SkinPlayerName on a spawn egg reliably applies that player's skin
Plain spawn eggs still roll a varied random skin as before

entries.title: PlayerMobs step over carriage gaps instead of leaping them
entries.summary: PlayerMobs crossing between train carriage groups now take a hop sized to the actual gap. Dungeon Train tightened the seams between carriages, but PlayerMobs kept using the same big sprint-leap they needed for the old wider gaps — so they'd sail across a hand's-width seam. They now step over it.
highlights: Cross-carriage hops are sized to the real gap — about half the height and half the distance at Dungeon Train's current spacing
Wider gaps still get the full sprint jump, so nothing changes where the longer leap is actually needed
Fixed a mob briefly getting stuck in its crossing state after landing on a very narrow gap

entries.title: PlayerMobs find their way back onto the train
entries.summary: A PlayerMob that falls onto the tracks now works its way back aboard instead of getting stuck. It bridges off the rails when there is a drop, builds a pillar up beside the passing carriages, and waits for a clear opening before jumping in.
highlights: Mobs stranded on the track bed no longer stand on the edge indefinitely — they place a block and step off.
Mobs beside the line build straight up rather than pacing alongside the train.
Boarding waits for a genuine opening, so mobs stop leaping into carriage walls or through gaps.
A mob with nothing to build from is given a few planks so it can bridge out and climb back on.

entries.title: PlayerMobs swim to shore and climb back to the train
entries.summary: A PlayerMob knocked off the train into water used to bob where it landed until the train left it behind — it could not even start trying to recover while afloat. It now swims properly, makes for the nearest reachable bank, and works its way back toward the line. Where the track runs on pillars it will walk up an existing spiral staircase rather than building its own.
highlights: Mobs that fall in the water now swim out instead of treading water until the train is gone
They swim at a player's pace and with the player swimming stroke, rather than paddling upright at walking speed
They head for the nearest bank they can actually climb out onto, preferring low ground near the track over a distant or sheer shoreline
Where a staircase or ladder already runs up to the track, they use it instead of pillaring up beside it

entries.title: PlayerMobs no longer empty shulker boxes they pick up
entries.summary: A PlayerMob (or an Echo) that picked up your shulker box would wipe everything inside it — when you killed the mob to get the box back, it came back empty. The mob was treating the box as a plain building block and re-placing it as an empty one. Now it keeps shulker boxes intact: it will still carry one and drop it when it dies, but never places it or uses it as building material, so the contents always survive.
highlights: Shulker boxes picked up by a PlayerMob keep their contents
A mob still carries a shulker box and returns it intact when killed
PlayerMobs never place shulker boxes as bridge, recovery, or combat-cover blocks

entries.title: Fighting back no longer marks you as a killer
entries.summary: When you die, the echo you leave behind is shaped by how you treated the people you met — but until now it couldn't tell murder from survival. Kills where something came for you first now count for a tenth as much, so a life spent defending yourself reincarnates near neutral instead of as a monster.
highlights: Damage and kills against a mob that targeted or struck you first are weighed at 10% toward both Fight/Flight and Friendliness.
Your own first strike still counts in full — the discount only applies once the other side has picked the fight.
Hate-seeded death-note echoes hunt you, so cutting one down barely stains the life you leave behind.

entries.title: Not fighting an echo back makes your own echo flighty
entries.summary: Your echo used to be shaped only by the violence you did. Now it is also shaped by the violence you refused. An echo that comes for you and doesn't get a fight out of you leaves its mark: take its blows without hitting back, or slip away from it alive, and the echo born from your death leans toward Flight. Hit it back even once — or kill it — and the whole credit is handed straight back. A fight once joined is a fight.
highlights: Damage you take from an echo you never strike back counts toward Flight, point for point against damage you deal.
Getting away clean from an echo that was hunting you counts too, once per echo.
One blow in return, or the kill, cancels everything that echo had earned you.
A life that never raised a hand used to reincarnate as a fighter; now it comes back timid.

entries.title: Order the PlayerMob you named — or nobody
entries.summary: Commands that take a PlayerMob name have always fallen back to the nearest mob when nothing matched, which means an order aimed at a name that no longer exists lands on a bystander. Two new options put you in control: exact-name matching, and quiet failures for orders driven by automation.
highlights: /playermob exactnames on — a <name> that matches no loaded PlayerMob cancels the command instead of falling back to the nearest one. Off by default, so nothing changes until you turn it on.

/playermob orderfailures off — a /playermob order that cannot run is cancelled silently instead of explaining itself in red chat. Handy when orders come from a chat bot or command block and the errors are just noise. On by default.
Both are also config keys (exactNames, orderFailureMessages) in config/playermob.properties, and the command form is a session override.

entries.title: Turn PlayerMob scavenging off — or limit it to wild mobs
entries.summary: PlayerMobs raid chests, strip armor stands and hoover up loose items. Three new config settings let you decide who does what: leave it on for everyone, switch it off entirely, or restrict it to PlayerMobs that spawned into the world on their own, so the ones you summon as companions leave your base storage alone.
highlights: New config settings searchContainers, searchArmorStands and collectFloorItems, each one of enabled / disabled / onlynaturallyspawning (default enabled — nothing changes unless you change it)
onlynaturallyspawning lets wild, chunk-generation, spawner and Dungeon-Train PlayerMobs keep scavenging while spawn-egg, /summon and dispenser mobs don't
Each behaviour is separate — you can stop chest raiding while still letting mobs pick up gear off the floor
Change any of them live with /playermob searchcontainers|searcharmorstands|collectflooritems <mode>

entries.title: Your pets come back with you
entries.summary: The animals you tamed are remembered when you die, and up to three of them return alongside your echo — loyal to it, exactly as they were to you. They follow it down the train, teleport to it when they fall behind, and turn on anyone who attacks it. Mounts stay behind unless you gave them a name; a horse you never named was transport, not a companion. Taming also counts as kindness, so a life spent befriending animals comes back friendlier than one that did not.
highlights: Up to three tamed animals return with an echo of the life that tamed them.
Returned pets follow, teleport and defend their echo like a living owner's pets — a PlayerMob is now a real owner as far as the game is concerned.
Unnamed mounts are left behind; a named one comes back.
Taming raises the friendliness the echo of that life is born with.

entries.title: PlayerMobs pick up dropped flint and steel
entries.summary: PlayerMobs now grab flint and steel they see lying on the ground and hold onto it, so they're ready to use it to light TNT in a fight.

entries.title: PlayerMobs cook their kills, torch their enemies, and put fires out
entries.summary: A PlayerMob carrying flint and steel now uses it the way you would — and, for the first time, reacts to fire instead of walking straight into it. It sets an animal alight just before the killing blow so the meat drops cooked, occasionally torches the ground under an enemy mid-fight, and stops short of a fire in its path to put it out. It always lights the block its target is standing on, with the tool actually drawn — never by magic.
highlights: Cooks its kills: an animal one swing from death gets the ground lit under it, dies burning, and drops cooked meat — then the fire is stamped back out a moment later
Torches enemies: against anything not already on fire it occasionally lights the ground under its target and leaves it burning, at most 5 times in 10 seconds
Draws the tool for real: a 4-20 tick swap in and out, and the fire is placed by right-clicking the block below its target, so rain and bad surfaces refuse it just like they would for you
Puts fires out: walking toward a fire it usually stops short, hesitates a beat, and punches it out — or empties a water bucket on it and scoops the water back if it carries one
Still fallible: it misses roughly one fire in four and walks in, then runs for water as before
